p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Yoga, originating in ancient India, is widely regarded as a practice integrating physical postures, breathing techniques, and meditation. Beyond its physical benefits, yoga emphasizes mental discipline, self-awareness, and holistic well-being. In modern contexts, yoga has been commodified, with fitness studios, branded courses, and online tutorials making it a global phenomenon. While such commercialization increases accessibility, it risks reducing yoga to mere exercise, detached from its philosophical and spiritual roots. Scientific studies suggest that consistent practice improves flexibility, cardiovascular health, stress management, and cognitive performance. However, casual adoption without proper guidance may cause physical strain or misinterpretation of principles. Governments and institutions increasingly promote yoga for public health and cultural diplomacy. Consequently, yoga occupies a dual role: as both a therapeutic practice and a symbol of cultural heritage, requiring balance between authenticity and contemporary adaptation.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The global agricultural sector faces a massive challenge: it must drastically scale food production to meet a growing population while simultaneously cutting its heavy environmental footprint under the pressures of climate change. The twentieth-century Green Revolution relied on intense inputs—using massive amounts of chemical fertilizers, synthetic pesticides, and groundwater pumping—which damaged soil ecology, depleted aquifers, and accelerated biodiversity loss. Continuing with this resource-heavy paradigm is ecologically impossible. Achieving sustainable food security requires adopting smart agricultural innovations, such as precision farming using IoT sensors, developing climate-resilient crop varieties that resist drought, and scaling agroecological farming systems. However, smallholder farmers, who produce the majority of food in developing countries, are often locked out of these technologies due to high costs and lack of credit. True agricultural resilience requires building equitable technology distribution frameworks, offering localized crop insurance against weather shocks, and protecting seed sovereignty for small farmers.

questions.q: Choose the correct inverted structure:
opts: No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out.
No sooner the bell had rung than the students rushed out.
No sooner did the bell rang than the students rushed out.
No sooner had the bell rung when the students rushed out.
questions.why: 'No sooner' takes inversion (had + subject + past participle) and pairs with 'than'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the error: “The list of approved candidates are displayed on the notice board.”
questions.why: The subject is 'list' (singular): 'is displayed'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “She ______ in this hospital since 2015.”
questions.why: An action from a past point continuing now, with 'since': present perfect (continuous). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: Seldom did I have met so honest an officer.
Seldom have I met so honest an officer.
Seldom have met I so honest an officer.
Seldom I have met so honest an officer.
questions.why: Negative adverbs (seldom, never, rarely) at the start take auxiliary + subject. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the error: “He has been living in Panaji for 2019.”
questions.why: Use 'since' with a point of time (2019); 'for' with a period (five years). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: India won the Men's Junior Asia Cup and retained the Women's Junior Asia Cup in 2026. Junior Asia Cups are age-group tournaments in:
If MARGAO is written as NBSHBP in a certain code, how is PANAJI written in that code?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: P-Q, A-B, N-O, A-B, J-K, I-J.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.why: The gaps grow by one each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6. O is the 15th letter, so the next is the 21st, U.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.why: Each term is double the previous one plus 1: 95 x 2 + 1 = 191.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.why: The terms are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 squared plus 1. The next is 6 squared plus 1 = 37.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 6, 18, 72, 360, ?
questions.why: The multipliers are 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6: 360 x 6 = 2160.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 100, 96, 88, 76, 60, ?
questions.why: The amounts subtracted are 4, 8, 12, 16, then 20: 60 - 20 = 40.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
questions.why: These are the prime numbers in order. The next prime after 13 is 17.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
questions.why: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 6, 11, 21, 36, 56, ?
questions.why: The differences are 5, 10, 15, 20, then 25: 56 + 25 = 81.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
questions.why: Each term is double the previous one minus 1: 33 x 2 - 1 = 65.

questions.q: Hahnemann's experiment of 1790, which led him to the law of similars, was made with:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. While translating Cullen's Materia Medica in 1790 he took cinchona himself and developed symptoms like intermittent fever.

questions.q: The observation that symptoms disappear from above downward, from within outward and in the reverse order of their appearance is known as:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Constantine Hering described this direction of cure.

questions.q: Treating a disease with the very agent or product that caused it is called:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hahnemann discussed isopathy in a note to §56 and did not accept it as true homoeopathy.

questions.q: The main source of the symptoms recorded in homoeopathic Materia Medica is:
opts: provings of drugs on healthy human beings
questions.why: Materia Medica is built chiefly from provings on healthy people, supplemented by toxicology and clinical observation.

questions.q: Crataegus oxyacantha mother tincture is used as an organ remedy for the:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. A heart tonic in clinical organ therapeutics.

questions.q: Ferrum phosphoricum is chiefly used in:
opts: the first stage of inflammations and fevers, before exudation
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ferrum phos: early inflammatory stage, haemorrhagic tendency.

questions.q: A sycotic remedy with fixed ideas, warts, and the sensation of something alive moving in the abdomen is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Thuja's fixed ideas and sensation of something alive in the abdomen.

questions.q: Medorrhinum is prepared from:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Psorinum = scabies vesicle; Syphilinum = chancre; Tuberculinum = TB material.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'p.r.n.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Pro re nata.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's concept of the 'complete symptom' includes location, sensation, modality and:
questions.why: The four elements of a complete symptom.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, the rubric for 'fear of death' is found in the chapter:

questions.q: Wrist drop results from injury to the:
questions.why: The radial nerve supplies the wrist extensors; it is often injured in shaft-of-humerus fractures.

questions.q: The normal tidal volume of an adult at rest is about:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About 150 mL of it is anatomical dead space.

questions.q: Caseous necrosis is characteristic of:
questions.why: Cheese-like necrosis within granulomas.

questions.q: Koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails) is a sign of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Leukonychia points to hypoalbuminaemia (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024).

questions.q: Under current Indian and international guidelines, hypertension in an adult is diagnosed at a clinic BP of at least:
questions.why: Confirmed on repeated readings.

questions.q: In a patient with Graves' disease, the thyroid profile shows (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Suppressed TSH with raised T3 and T4.

questions.q: Recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation, with altered stool frequency or form and no structural disease, is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Rome IV criteria for IBS; a functional disorder.

questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Thelarche usually comes first; menarche comes about 2 years later.

questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Oedema is the hallmark of kwashiorkor.

questions.q: The first step in managing a trauma victim is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
opts: securing the airway (with cervical spine protection)
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. ABC: airway first.

questions.q: For blunt injuries, bruises and a sore, bruised feeling after a fall, the first remedy is:

questions.q: The core principle of the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):

questions.q: The incidence of a disease measures:

questions.q: The infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of infants under one year per:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A sensitive indicator of community health.
